plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: Just as the garden fades into autumn, naked leafless stems shoot up topped with spidery clusters of ribbon-petalled, rose-pink blooms that shimmer with a frosty sparkle in low autumn light. Their candy-bright color glows against golden leaves and damp, cool days.
plants.bloomingSeason: September to October, peaking in early to mid-autumn
plants.location: Gardens in the United Kingdom and Ireland, and other temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens (native to South Africa)
plants.funFact: Although it is native to the mountains of South Africa, it thrives in cool northern gardens. It flowers best when its bulbs are baked in summer sun and left crowded at the surface of the soil.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest of all proteas, it has a dinner-plate-sized flower head, a crown of silky, pink-tipped bracts surrounding a central cushion of fuzzy, creamy florets. It is a bold, sculptural bloom that looks almost prehistoric among the fynbos shrubland.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring, roughly June to October in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Cape fynbos of South Africa, including the slopes around Cape Town and Kirstenbosch
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. Its tough, fire-adapted rootstock lets it resprout after the wildfires that regularly sweep through the fynbos.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Airy, feathery foliage carries daisy-like flowers with satiny petals that dance on slender stems in the breeze. In autumn, whole fields sway in waves of pink, magenta and white, a favorite sight for visitors to Japan's parks.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through autumn, with famous mass displays in Japan in October
plants.location: Autumn flower fields in Japan, such as Showa Kinen Park in Tokyo (native to Mexico)
plants.funFact: In Japan cosmos is called akizakura, meaning 'autumn cherry blossom', because its delicate pink flowers sway in fields in the way cherry blossoms do in spring.
